$comment: This is a ratchet, not an allowlist. Every entry is a LIVE defect that the
corrected scanner now detects and that predates it. Entries exist so that
unrelated pull requests are not blocked by a defect they did not introduce
— not to make the finding acceptable.
Rules the script enforces: an entry that no longer matches must be deleted,
every entry needs a reason and a trackedIn, and `maxEntries` caps the list
so it can only shrink. Growing it is a reviewed baseline change under
Entries are keyed file::rule, so a NEW hardcoded secret in an already-listed
file still fails if it trips a different rule — and the two rules covering
app/api/admin/auth/route.ts are listed separately for that reason.

entries.reason: Three staff accounts declared inline with a `password:` property. This is the exact syntax the previous grep could not match. Removing the array in favour of database-backed accounts is owned by a separate task.
All three accounts share the published bcrypt test-vector digest for the string 'password', with no NODE_ENV gate, so the staff login is open to anyone who has read the file or recognises the hash.

JWT_SECRET falls back to the literal 'your-secret-key', so any deployment missing that variable signs and accepts admin tokens anyone can forge. The fix is to throw on a missing secret rather than substitute one.
